課程概述:
This graduate-level seminar explores the intersection of Accounting Information Systems, data analytics, and emerging artificial intelligence technologies within accounting and auditing contexts. The course is structured as a research-oriented seminar emphasizing critical discussion and analytical engagement with academic literature.

The seminar covers topics including eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL), text mining, data visualization, and AIS literature reading that addresses machine learning, artificial intelligence, and large language models. A central objective of the AIS-DA Seminar is to guide students in learning how to read and interpret accounting, auditing, and AIS-related research papers, become familiar with academic writing conventions, and explore potential directions for their master’s thesis. Through sustained engagement with selected studies, students will develop the ability to understand research motivation, evaluate empirical design choices, and reflect on how technological developments shape new research opportunities.
課程目標:
The AIS serial courses, Accounting Information Systems with Data Analytics at the undergraduate level and Seminar on Accounting Information Systems and Data Analytics at the graduate level, are designed to connect emerging technological developments with both professional practice and academic research in accounting and auditing. The graduate seminar places particular emphasis on cultivating students’ capacity to critically interpret and evaluate both foundational and contemporary research in the field.

Through sustained engagement with research addressing areas such as XBRL, textual analysis, data visualization, machine learning, and generative artificial intelligence, students will examine how technological change influences financial reporting, assurance processes, and the broader information environment. Rather than focusing solely on technical implementation, the seminar encourages careful analysis of theoretical motivation, research design, and identification logic. Students are guided to consider how evolving technologies open new avenues for inquiry while also raising new methodological questions.

By the conclusion of the semester, students should demonstrate greater confidence in analytical reading, more sophisticated participation in scholarly discussion, and a clearer sense of how to formulate research questions relevant to their own thesis development.

課程概述:
This is an advanced laboratory course in analog, digital, and mixed-signal electronic circuits, intended for students who have already completed the Electronics Laboratory course and wish to deepen both their theoretical understanding and practical skills. The course emphasizes rigorous circuit analysis, systematic design, careful implementation, and high-quality experimental verification. 
Throughout the semester, students will be expected to connect device-level behavior with system-level performance, quantify non-idealities (noise, distortion, finite bandwidth, quantization, etc.), and document their findings in professional-style technical reports. The course is suitable only for students who are seriously interested in electronic circuit design and measurement and are prepared to invest significant time on labs outside of scheduled lectures (self-paced).
Grading: Midterm 35%, Final 35%, Lab & project 30%
The tentative weekly syllabus:
1.	Advanced Lab practices and review
2.	Op-amp non-idealities & precision amplifiers
3.	Op-amp noise
4.	Signal conditioning for data acquisition
5.	Feedback, stability, and compensation
6.	Advanced oscillation circuits, timing jitter and stability
7.	Regulators & buck converters
8.	Midterm Exam
9.	Power management and PSRR, power noise
10.	Digital logic families, timing, and signal integrity
11.	Data converters and practical sampling issues
12.	Digital interfaces & MCU
13.	Low-noise interfaces
14.	Project I: design proposal for sensor nodes with ADC + MCU + communication interface
15.	Project II: Implementation & presentation
16.	Final Exam
課程目標:
By the end of this course, students should be able to:
1.	Apply advanced circuit theory to the analysis and design of analog and digital building blocks, including precision amplifiers, active filters, oscillators, comparators, and digital logic subsystems.
2.	Design, implement, and debug moderately complex analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits that meet specified performance targets, using both simulation tools (e.g., SPICE) and hardware prototypes.
3.	Characterize circuit performance experimentally, including gain, bandwidth, stability, distortion, noise, propagation delay, and power consumption, and relate measured results to analytical and simulated predictions.
4.	Evaluate and manage non-ideal effects such as parasitics, loading, biasing errors, power-supply limitations, signal integrity issues, and measurement uncertainty in practical laboratory environments.
課程要求: Completion of Experiments on Electronics (電子學實驗AM7011) and familiar with SPICE-based circuit simulation.

課程概述: 本課程旨在探討活細胞如何維持內在平衡、處理與整合資訊、產生機械力，並適應不斷變化的環境。本課程將分為兩個部分。第一部分建立現代細胞生理學的核心概念，強調不同細胞反應如何在時間與空間上被協調與整合。第二部分則介紹用於探究細胞生理機制的細胞生物學研究技術。
課程目標:
在修畢本課程後，學生將能夠：
1.	理解支持細胞生理運作的核心原則。
2.	整合細胞膜、胞器、代謝、訊號傳遞與機械性調控的相關知識。
3.	具批判性地閱讀細胞生理相關的研究文獻。
4.	運用現代細胞生物學研究技術來檢驗以細胞生理問題為導向的假說。

課程概述:
文化交流不論在博物館展覽或者學術研究上都是重要議題，絲路上的文化交流尤其引人入勝。本課程將由西元一至八世紀的東亞遺址和遺物出發，追索其與中亞、北亞相似遺址的關係，以探討絲路上的文化交流。課程包含授課教師講授、課堂討論，以及個人口頭與書面報告。

課程分為三個單元。第一單元為「緒論」（第一到第四週），首先在第一週介紹絲路研究背景、目前各大博物館的收藏及其他研究資源，也將一起思考文物歸屬議題。在第二和三週，以今阿富汗以及新疆地區的尼雅遺址作為實例，說明前一週所介紹的博物館藏品的部分出土地，同時介紹如何閱讀發掘報告。第三週則討論文化交流研究方法。目前討論文化交流的理論多由近現代世界文化交流出發，因此將在第三週簡介各理論並探討其在絲路文化交流上的適用性。也希望在整門課中，同學能時刻留意近現代文化交流與本課程所處的一到八世紀文化交流的異同，並嘗試尋找更合適的研究方法、取徑與理論。

第二單元為「遺物與遺址」從第五到第十三週，以大家相對熟悉的中國遺址與遺物出發，討論這些遺跡和絲路上其他地區的交流。第二單元的每堂課有兩個
課程目標:
。首先是對遺址和遺物基本資訊的掌握，包含熟悉各遺址出土的遺物類型和風格、遺址重要性，以及學者針對這些遺址與遺物提出的問題與解決問題的方法。其次，針對各週介紹的遺物進行視覺分析。

第三單元為「專題討論」，從第十四週開始，每週以一類物質或主題進行跨越地理區域的討論，探討圖像、紋飾與技術在長距離交流上的可能媒介、動力與可能造成的意義轉變。
課程目標
期待課程結束後，學生能夠達到以下目標：
1.認識本課程討論之遺址與遺物和其所處的歷史與社會背景、了解目前學界研究成果，並且從中提出新的研究問題。
2.掌握文化交流研究方法，並且有能力洞察學者討論文化交流時的前提假設。在本學期中以每週的實例思考各理論與研究方法的適用性與限制，並拓展其他可能性。
3.學習分析、比較遺物與遺址的能力。要能探討是獨立發明，或者可能有文化交流，並清楚解釋自己如何判別。
4.增進口頭與書面報告能力。
5.學習搜集與閱讀考古報告，從中取得需要的資訊，以在期末報告中回答自己提出的研究問題。
6.掌握國際學界對絲路研究的動向，並拓展國際視野。
課程要求: 課程進行方式以同學報告和討論為主，教師講授為輔。前四週由教師導讀，從第五週開始，每堂課由同學或教師導讀一到兩篇當週

課程概述: This course aims to teach the fundamentals and applications of glycobiology in the broader context of functional glycomics, based on the recently updated textbook “essentials of glycobiology 2nd edition”, which is freely available on the ncbi bookshelf, and other web materials on the nature functional glycomics gateway. From the cause and consequences of onco-developmental changes in glycosylation to proteins that recognize, bind and mediate the functions of glycans, students are introduced to essential concepts and recent developments in the field. Current pursue in both basic research and medical applications, including the historical development of neuraminidase inhibitors (e.g. tamiflu) and glycans involved in viral infections are discussed in the context of what chemical approaches are available to glycobiologists for diagnostics and therapeutics. Seminars are organized for students in groups to present and discuss key original research papers, which together with following up written report, will constitute the principal course work and assessment.

課程概述:
綠色革命以來，全球農業發展已多聚焦於探討近代農業工業化、規模化、市場化與生產集中化所產生的後果，對生態環境、鄉村發展、社會文化、經濟安全所造成的影響。在這些有關探討農業發展的論述中，「農業生態學」提供了一個完整的理論架構，讓我們了解構成農業生態系統（agroecosystem）的結構脈絡。儘管農業生態學在早期主要應用於作物生產與農業生態，致力於研究、診斷、和提出一個有別於慣行農業典範的另類管理方法。但在最近的幾十年中，「農業生態學」被社會科學整合性的概念和方法所豐富，因此這個領域隨後演變成為一個立基於系統性的、跨學科的多維途徑，以幫助我們更好地理解獨特的社會和文化背景下出現的農業複雜性。
當我們將農業發展放在農業生態系統的架構與脈絡下，這個概念不僅為理解農業系統的各個組成部分之間的相互作用和關係提供了基礎，它的全系統（whole-systems）方法和動態平衡（dynamic equilibrium）視野更為「永續性」（sustainability）的討論提供了理論基礎。換言之，當我們試圖尋求一個另類的農業典範，除了永續發展的原則以及生態完整性，經濟活力和社會平等的相互依存關係可以幫助我們進行了解必要的變革，意即在生態、經濟、與社會的永續發展基礎下，建立並打造一個「韌性社會」為目標。
課程目標: (1)了解農業生態學與永續農業的核心概念與理論內容；(2)了解發生在當代農業典範中，相關於環境、經濟、與社會永續發展的問題和辯論，以及這些變化和趨勢對未來農業發展有什麼影響；(3)透過研究論文、科普文章、以及課程討論與分享，希望同學們逐漸拓展對於農業生態系統與永續化發展目標的分析、詮釋、與批判性思考。

課程概述:
聲音在當前的數位媒體環境中，已成為極為重要且具說服力的敘事形式。本學期的「數位傳播專題一」課程，將專注於「Podcast 製作與聲音敘事」。課程將探討聲音作為公共溝通之媒介角色，並結合新聞事實與敘事創意表達，引導學生以Podcast為載體，探索真實議題、人物故事與文化經驗現象。課程透過講授、工作坊與實作訓練，使學生們同時具備聲音節目規劃、錄製、剪輯與發布的技術與敘事能力。

In the digital media era, sound has re-emerged as one of the most intimate and persuasive storytelling forms. This course, offered under the series Audiovisual Media Topics, focuses this semester on Podcast Production and Audio Storytelling. It examines how sound functions as a medium for public communication and creative journalism. Students will explore how to combine journalistic accuracy with narrative imagination, using podcasts as a platform to convey real-world issues, human experiences, and cultural stories.
Through lectures, workshops, and hands-on production, students will gain both technical and creative skills in podcast planning, recording, editing, and publishing.
課程目標:
修課學生預期能夠：
1.	理解 Podcast 與聲音敘事的媒介特性、社會功能與文化意涵。
2.	能從現實議題中發掘主題，設計敘事結構並完成具公共性的聲音節目。
3.	熟悉採訪、錄音、剪輯與混音等製作流程，掌握 Podcast 節目製作的基本技術能力。
4.	培養媒體倫理意識與公共表達責任，理解聲音作為公共溝通工具的角色。
5.	產出可於系所或公開平台播出的專業 Podcast 節目，展現結合理論與實作的整合能力。

By the end of the course, students will be able to:
1.	Understand the media characteristics, social functions, and cultural significance of podcasting and audio storytelling.
2.	Identify real-world issues and transform them into structured and engaging narrative audio programs.
3.	Develop technical proficiency in interviewing, recording, editing, and mixing to produce professional podcast content.
4.	Cultivate media ethics and a sense of public responsibility in using sound as a form of civic communication.
5.	Produce a professional-level podcast suitable for publication on institutional or public platforms, demonstrating the integration of theory and creative practice.

課程概述: 在全球數位科技快發展(包含人工智慧)、氣候變遷、跨境人口流動及跨境人畜共通疾病的快速流通下，何謂鄉村？何謂都市？已經成為地理學、社會學以及人類學的重要論辯。而數位基礎設施，包含海底電䌫、低軌衛星、資料中心、物流中心、社交媒體的快速發展，進一步挑戰了都市/鄉村這樣的傳統劃界。也因此，本課程主要為從鄉村視角出發，來看到在數位科技快速發展下，我們如何界定鄉村和都市的新型態關係。因此，本課程主要分要二大部份：第一部份主要聚焦在近年來都市和鄉村關係的論辯，包含了行星都市化(Planetary urbanization)、鄉村化(ruralization)以及行星鄉村地理學等；而這一部份，也包含了晚近關於「領域」(territory)、邊界(border)以及區域(region)等的論辯。而第二部份的焦點則放在新型態的數位基礎護施的發展，如何複雜化了都市和鄉村的分界。包含了海底電纜、資料中心、人工智慧晶片製造、數位媒體等，如何重塑都市和鄉村關係。
課程目標:
1、增加學生理解國際當前國際學術前沿的廣度。
2、提升掌握學生學術文獻論點的能力。
課程要求: 本課程各週都有一定的指定專書、期刊閱讀，且需固定繳交批判性閱讀摘要，是閱讀、討論密集的課程。所有參與的同學都需盡到上述這些責任。

課程概述:
本課程為學年課程。本學期課程內容將含括邀請產、官、學專家進行學術演講，分享其學術研究成果；期初－研究初探分享；期中－研究議題進度報告；期末－研究成果報告。

【作業繳交規定】
※第一部分：專家學術演講
1).每兩位同學一組，需負責一位專家前來演講的所有事前準備、事後整理、報導撰寫，報導請於課後周四中午12點前寄給明心助教。
2).每次演講後，繳交心得一篇。繳交時間為每場演講後的周四中午12點前上傳CEIBA；主旨：【專討演講心得報告】－學號－姓名，逾期視為缺交。請以WORD軟體繕打心得，字級限12級字，細明體，行距單行，字數不限。 

※第二部分：期中－研究議題進度報告
1).以PPT報告方式進行，上台口頭報告時之課程時間將延長。基本上碩士生一人報告15分鐘，問答6分鐘；博士生一人報告20分鐘，問答10分鐘（可能依修課人數有所調整）。報告順序請至公佈欄查詢。
2).5月5日中午12點前繳交，至少1,000字報告書及PPT至CEIBA。未準時繳交，視為遲交。內容須含括：本學期研究議題與構想、計畫摘要或接續上學期專題討論課程研究計畫之進度。
3).5月6日繳交書面（報告書、PPT檔）資料給任課教師與助教。內容須含括：本學期研究議題與構想、計畫摘要或接續上學期專題討論課程研究計畫之進度。


※第三部分：期末－研究成果報告
1).以PPT報告方式進行，9:30開始上課，碩士生一人報告20分鐘，問答7分鐘；博士生一人報告25分鐘，問答12分鐘（可能依修課人數有所調整）。
2).6月16日中午12點前繳交，至少5,000字報告書（含背景、動機、目的、重要性、文獻回顧、研究設計、研究成果、參考文獻書目並符合APA格式，若未達到要求，視為缺交）及PPT至CEIBA。未準時繳交，視為遲交。
3).6月17日繳交書面（報告書、PPT檔）資料給任課教師與修課同學。內容須含括：鼓勵以完整研究進行報告，若未完成須提出至研究設計階段；若未達到要求，視同缺交作業。

1).請同學與指導教授進行討論，並以個人可能研究方向做準備。

課程概述:
前沿檢測技術： 探討次世代定序（NGS）與全基因組定序（WGS）在食品溯源與爆發監測中的關鍵角色，以及 CRISPR 系統在病原菌精準偵測的應用。

系統生物學應用： 解析如何利用蛋白質組學與代謝組學，動態監測食品發酵過程或腐敗菌的生化路徑。

智慧化食品安全： 介紹大數據與 AI 模型如何預測微生物生長動力學，並結合物聯網（IoT）達成食品供應鏈的即時監控。

未來趨勢： 研討合成生物學在機能性益生菌開發中的潛力，以及減碳趨勢下的新型食品防腐技術。
課程目標: 本課程旨在引領修課同學跳脫傳統微生物培養的框架，深入探索食品微生物學的數位化與精準化轉型。隨著科技迭代，現代食微研究已進入「多體學（Omics）」與「人工智慧」並行的時代。本課程不僅提供知識的更新，更著重於培養學生將創新科技轉化為產業解決方案的能力。透過國內外最新文獻研討，學子將能掌握未來十年食品產業在微生物品質控管與機能開發的核心競爭力。
課程要求: 對於食品科技與微生物應用需有相關背景知識。
預期學習時數: 課前閱讀與課後複習，各2小時/周。

課程概述: 本課程目的為協助學生了解運動場域中的性別議題，藉由課程講授、專題講座及討論等方式提供學生論述與實務經驗的連結，並透過自我經驗反思、運動歷史與運動時事的評析培養學生對體育運動中性別不平等現況的覺察能力，提升性別意識並建立批判及獨立思考能力。藉由課程講授、運動時事討論、專題講演等形式，逐步培養學生在運動參與過程中的性別敏銳度。
課程目標:
1.	透過不同主題及運動時事引導學生進行運動參與經驗時的反思。
2.	藉由實際事例與討論引導學生覺察體育運動中性別不平等現況/事件。
3.	協助學生習得性別概念、提昇性別意識、發展問題解決策略，以培養學生破除運動性別意識形態的能力。

課程概述:
學 分 數：3 學分，本課程每梯次實習 120 小時，依假期安排微調整個時程。
實習時間：分兩梯次實習，第一梯次為115年05月19日-115年06月12日。第二梯次為115年06月15日-115年07月10日。每梯次實習120 小時，於每週二、三、四、五全天實習(8:00-16:30)，詳細病房實習時間見各梯次安排的實習計畫表單。
實習場所：台大醫院(雲林分院)精神醫學部急性病房、門診、日間病房、社區居家訪視。
課程目標:
一、實習目標
    (一)確認臨床常見的精神疾病症狀，並熟悉相關的治療。
    (二)運用溝通技巧及人際關係理論與病患及家屬建立治療性關係。
    (三)學習以生理、心理、智能、社會及靈性五大層面評估與確立病患的護理問題。   
    (四)瞭解不同病情階段病患的護理需求，應用護理過程，訂定計劃並執行有效之
        護理措施。
    (五)學習與醫療團隊成員建立協同合作關係。
    (六)運用危機治療、團體治療、環境治療及個別心理治療的概念護理個案及家屬。  
    (七)運用精神衛生護理相關法律議題與倫理考量於個案護理。
    (八)促進自我了解與自我成長。
課程要求:
考核方式與作業
   (一) 臨床實習考核 65 %：考核標準見【附件一實習成績考核表】。

古典散文與文人生活密不可分，涉及時代語境的種種變化，不僅可作為政治語彙的操作，也可視為個人情意感知的具體呈顯。然而，古典散文之文體成規也是我們在解讀文本時不可忽略之問題，分類是我們面對古典散文時不可迴避之學術課題，何種文體在怎樣的社會語境中佔據了我們的視野，同時也意味著文人核心關懷的座落之處。
本課程為一年課程，主要依循時代脈絡規劃範圍，各時代關懷主題的變化則是課程規劃的第二項考量。除了具體的文學文本之外，本課程亦將藉由不同的學術論著協助各位掌握學界研究脈絡。
課程目標:
1.訓練學生精讀與分析文本的能力。
2.掌握古典散文之生成語境及衍生議題。
3.理解學術研究之基本規範與討論方式。。
4.藉由文本細讀與分析，深掘文本內涵，進一步建構文體發展之軌跡。
課程要求:
1.本課程重視文本預習，課程講授以了解相關主題、學術研究的關懷旨趣，上課前請務必閱讀該週文本。
2.本課程除了期中、期末考之外，另有兩次習作。

課程概述:
本課程為中文系二年級必修課程。我們將接續先秦兩漢文（即中文系一年級本系國文所授），陸續講解魏晉唐宋明清諸朝代的辭賦和文章。
案自兩漢以來、歷經魏晉南朝隋唐，在各級政府擔任掾屬職位的文人集團形成後，「文」便同「詩」般坐穩首要文體的位置。且正因文家掌秘書職司的緣故，「文」的品種遂環繞官場諸多情狀展開：從鋪敘朝章典儀的頌讚、箴戒當權毋荒淫懈怠的諷諫，到發揮勸慰勵志、瀉懣或解嘲功能的騷賦，還有流通諸公、私領域，左右諸人際關係的形色文章；又隨著重學問、崇典籍、尚雅麗工整，追求得體、妥當等秘書文化的逐步成熟，對辭語、章句、典故、對仗、用韻等的要求遂一一確立，培訓、揀擇人才乃至文壇品評的標準盡在其中。凡此種種，我們將於前半學期透過諸篇選文，解說這些浸染掾屬文化色彩的辭賦和文章該怎麼讀、怎麼理解，又當如何鑒賞。
到了下半學期，我們將討論唐宋古文運動，還有綿延宋元明清諸朝的文章學。透過揭示前者的核心主張，若「學文養氣」：亦即藉諷詠聖賢遺文好涵濡性情、擴充胸次氣象以待吐辭垂訓的論述，還有剖析後者大力發展的，重點在編選所謂的大家文文集且施以評註、圈點，好開發文脈錯綜接合論述的學問，我們非但能進入從前那自開蒙即勤練文章、終生仕途亦唯憑斯藝的時代，漸次了解諸文派所以更相迭代，諸文家又多有理學或心學背景的道理；更重要的是，我們將擺脫白話文運動的偏見，重新學會品味、評論諸作品自民族精神到卓越技藝的多面價值。總之，藉下半學期諸選文及其施諸其上的評點的講解，我們或能較公允地評述古文文化的相關成就。
課程目標:
1.學習解讀並鑒賞掾屬文化的詞章。
2.學習解讀並鑒賞古文運動後的詞章。

課程概述:
透過形式與韻律，詩人將抽象卻真實的情感以文字定形，而情感的發生，可能來自外物的觸動、人情的感知、事件的衝擊、社會現象的觀察或個人處境際遇的盤桓思索。因此讀詩的過程，也正是一個興、觀、群、怨的交感過程，引領讀者以新的心眼，觀看世界、體察人情、認知自我，並從中習得如何筆補造化，將漫漶的情感、缺憾的現實，以詩精煉而節制、超越而圓滿的體現。
    詩選及習作為中文系必修課程，課綱規畫以時代為經，詩歌形式與題材為緯，依序閱讀中國詩歌史上的經典名篇，藉此建構中國詩歌發展歷程的整體認知，同時透過文本的精密閱讀、創作背景的考察，品味詩歌節奏韻律與形式結構之美，體察詩人寄寓於詩歌的情感經驗、際遇思索、人性體會。讀詩之外，課程並訓練古典詩歌寫作，上下學期分別進行古體詩及近體詩習作。
    本學期接續上學期進度，繼續選讀魏晉、南北朝及唐代名家詩歌。
課程目標:
1、	透過詩歌文本精密解讀，深入詩歌世界，與詩心交遊，涵養共情同理的本能與悲憫襟懷。

3、	在古典詩的習作中，體驗詩人寫詩的用心及過程，嘗試發掘個人創作天賦與熱情。

課程概述:
詞之為體，鏗鏘曼妙，是配合音樂而能歌唱的詩。詞人所代表的是一種細膩、敏感的生命型態。追憶往事，流連光景，對於男女相思之情、風物年華之變化，詞人多出之以輕靈細緻的筆觸，寫入哀感，賦以真情，最能動人心魂，予人隱約淒迷之感。而詞的體製，如樂律章節之重複節奏、文辭句法的平衡對稱，更強化了這種婉轉低回、留連反覆的情感質性。
詞的世界，是一個有情的世界。唐宋詞以長歌短調、清辭麗句，抒發人間情誼，表現為沉重的或輕淡的、溫柔的或熱情的姿貌，既具古典美，又富浪漫情，值得細細吟詠。
古人，因時感事而作詞；今我，緣情興感而讀詞─古往今來，牽繫著彼此的就是變化人生之中那不變的情誼。以今情讀古詞，讀的不只是唐宋名家的情意，其實更能讀到一己的內在情思。如是，時空交感，彼此同心，我們的情感天地顯得深美、更渾厚、更寬廣。
本課程以選讀唐宋名家詞為主，希望透過對不同時代、題材、風格、流派的作品之研讀，了解詞的演進發展，欣賞詞體之美、人情之美，豐富我們對傳統抒情美典的認識。同時，在賞讀之餘，學習詞的寫作，以體察古人之用心，加強一己對中國文字聲情之美的體認。
課程目標:
(一) 辨體以識情─教導同學以統合內外緣因素、兼顧內容與形式的完整文體觀，充分體察詞作為獨特的抒情文體的「辭」「情」特質。
(二) 同情與共感─以一種「以情感喚起情感」的解讀方式，帶領同學藉由生命情調的分享，加深對人文精神的體認，及對一己內在心靈世界的感知。
(三) 意義的探尋─從詞人創作的歷程、文體的抉擇、風格的轉變，以及詞體與時運的關聯等方面，對詞體本身的美學與倫理意涵作批判性的理解，並探問其現代意義。

課程概述: 本課程依據中國古典小說發展的特質，分文言小說和白話小說兩個系統於上下學期講授。關於文言小說的範疇主要按照小說發展的脈絡，擇取六朝志怪志人小說、唐代傳奇和明清筆記具代表性的作品研讀，藉以闡述其孳生背景、文類特質和其間的傳承關係。而白話小說的部分則以宋元話本、明代擬話本為講授主體，分別由其所納含的主題，例如命運、情欲、性別等，探討相關的佳作，進而彰顯文本思維的社會和個體之意義。

課程概述: 本課程為學年課，下學期以「明傳奇」為教授範圍。中國戲劇史上，明代是「戲文-傳奇」體製形成、發展、達至顛峰的重要階段，彼時劇作家輩出、作品數量繁多、演出興盛、各地腔調劇種紛立；劇本文學與劇場藝術皆呈現出多元而日趨精緻的面貌。本課程內容以「明傳奇」為主，研讀重點為湯顯祖《牡丹亭》，初步勾勒傳奇與崑劇表裡依傍的輪廓。
課程目標: 授課內容以「劇本賞析」為主體，為使同學對於戲劇的形式、內容有全面性的認知，重要劇作將閱讀「全本」，部分經典則以「選折」方式精解。透過對「文本」的研讀，理解傳統文人或伶人的「編劇技法」與「人物塑造」。時而配合相關內容的演出欣賞，以領略戲劇的重要本質：劇場與表演藝術。影片欣賞可感受當代演員、編劇、導演的「二度詮釋」，理解如何活化經典，進而明白傳統可透過當代意識更新與創發。希望同學們體會「案頭」與「場上」並重、「文學」與「劇場」兼美的意義。

課程概述:
本課乃在介紹《老子》的智慧。嘗試闡發老子的人生智慧，而主從符號（名）與自我（身，包含身體）的角度切入探索，瞭解自我在思想、感官和欲望上的問題，以助實踐完滿幸福的人生。

1. 前部份以〈道經〉三十七章為主進行教學，主在由形下而形上、由事而道的進行理解。

課程概述:
本課程限定中文系國際學生學士班選修。課程擬探討十九世紀以降臺灣社會與文化蓬勃多元的發展生態。本課程將從三個單元綜觀臺灣文學所涵蓋的族群、歷史、性別、政治、都市等議題，透過對作家和文本世界的發掘，進而認識和想像臺灣。
   「家國歷史與創傷記憶」單元選擇臺灣歷史上動盪記憶與傷痕印記：從大航海時代、日治到戰後臺灣的變遷，突出臺灣文學對歷史變遷與創傷記憶的深沈銘刻，以及在家國意識的徘徊和辯證。
   「族群政治與性別想像」單元透過外省、本省、原住民及新住民等族群議題的文本，揭示文學如何遊走臺灣的不同歷史階段，見證族群意識的變遷和族群政治的衝突與矛盾。另外，1980年以降崛起的性別意識，不但改變了臺灣社會的面貌，也進一步改變了臺灣對兩性關係和性別自覺的寫作，成為認識臺灣文學不能略過的文學風景。
   「都市空間與日常政治」透過飲食、街道連動地方歷史，打開文學進入都市的文化路徑，展現日常的身份敘事和庶民空間。

課程概述:
In this course, I will introduce theoretical and empirical analysis of social networks. Reflected by the rapidly growing number of network studies in different economic fields, such as in labor, health, development, international, and financial economics, social (or economic) networks have now become attractive and must-know subjects for graduate students in economics, particularly when data become widely available in this big data era.   
 
We will begin this course by learning the characterization of networks. Then we will visit the theoretical literature on games on networks. Next, we will discuss various empirical approaches for network data, including network sampling, community (cluster) detection, modeling network (spillover) effects, network formation, etc. Before the end of this course, we will discuss policy implications from a few classic network studies.
課程目標:
After completing this course, students should be:
1.	Acquainted with basic terminologies in social and economic network analysis.
2.	Familiar with the theoretical development of network games
3.	Able to perform econometric regressions on network data and provide economic interpretations.
4.	Able to use software R to collect data and conduct network analysis.

課程概述:
Practicum in English is one of the foundational courses for those who are interested in English language teaching. It builds on Teaching Methods and Materials in English, and is a prerequisite course for your six-month internship, which together will help you prepare for your future language teaching career.

The syllabus presented here is a tentative schedule for the spring semester. The course will be divided into three parts: 1) lectures and workshops, 2) school visits, and 3) the English Enhancement Program (EEP) teaching practicum. See more details below.

1)	Lectures and workshops
This part will mostly be facilitated by Professor Giles Witton-Davies from W1 to W8. Please refer to the weekly schedule.

2)	School visits
Six school visits will be arranged between W9 and W14 (the time of the visits, however, will depend on the availability of the teachers, which means that it could be during any time of the week; if a school visit is arranged that week, there is no need to meet on Tuesday evening). This is a wonderful opportunity to observe how secondary school teachers teach. You are expected to attend at least four visits.

3)	EEP teaching practicum
The EEP teaching practicum, running from mid-March to the end of May, will be primarily arranged by the Center for Bilingual Education. Each person will be teaching twice; please refer to your selected time slot here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/17YG-zpmBdMtv50ErRFJB7XTJ_loa3n4jgSRqJ8tQ8S0/edit?tab=t.0
課程目標:
By the end of this course, you will:
•	Become more aware of the everyday realities of teaching.
•	Enhance your skills in lesson planning, course design, and teaching.
•	Continue engaging in dialogues that deal with the tensions between theory and practice.
課程要求:
Be professional. In the spring semester, you will go through a major identity transformation: from being a student to being an early career teacher. This transformation can be quite overwhelming, but see it as an invaluable opportunity to develop your professional identity as a teacher.

Being professional in the teaching context means being on time, wearing proper clothing (e.g., no sandals; avoid jeans; shirt with collar always best), taking your work seriously (e.g., plan, practice, reflect, and revise), engaging in teaching conversations (e.g., ask questions and share what you know), and seeking continuous growth (e.g., find inspirations from observing, reading, attending workshops).

For all school visits, please also:
•	Bring a notebook to take notes with a pen (refrain from using electronic devices when visiting schools, especially during observation and post-observation discussion)
•	Prepare questions to ask the teachers during post-observation discussion

Observation analysis

You are asked to choose one area to systematically focus on in every observation, including the EEP course (when you are the TA) and the school visits. The area could be teacher-student and student-student interactions; design and implementation of pedagogical activities; the use of technology in teaching; classroom management; teaching speaking, listening, reading, or writing; teaching grammar and vocabulary; or assessment (it would be a good idea to have another area in mind, just in case the area you’ve chosen does not “appear” in the observed classes). During the observations, you may take notes of whatever you find most meaningful, but please pay special attention to the specific area that you’ve chosen. For the observation report, you are asked to write, in English, a three-page analysis that includes the following: 1) why you’ve selected the particular area to zoom into; 2) how this area was manifested in at least four of the observed classes; and 3) which teacher(s) you think handled that area exceptionally well and why. 課程概述:
Principle of Communications is the first course to communication systems for undergraduate students, and it aims to uncover how a communication system works and the underlying beautiful theoretical principles. It builds the foundations for students to explore more advanced topics related to communications, ranging from theoretical development to practical implementation, such as wireless communications, wireless networks, Internet of Things, etc.. Lectures are developed to answer the following key question: how to reliably deliver information over an unreliable physical medium?

Towards answering this question, we begin with the interface between the cyber and the physical world and explain how to convert from digital to analog and vice versa. Next, we introduce a first statistical model, the additive noise channel, that captures the unreliable feature of physical medium, and develop the principle for optimal reconstruction based on statistical decision theory. Some concepts of compressing analog and digital information will be introduced for communicating or storing information on capacity limited medium. Then, we will introduce the key concept of coding in order to achieve reliable communication. These principles are extended to further channel models, namely, wireline (telephone) channel and wireless channel, where additional challenges such as inter-symbol interference (ISI) need to be tackled. Some system design concepts to counter or take advantage of the channel effects.

課程概述:
本研究所專題導向課程探討如何運用機器學習（ML）技術來解決電子設計自動化（EDA）中的 NP-complete 最佳化問題。學生將學習如何將典型的 EDA 問題建模為馬可夫決策過程（MDP），並開發可取代或輔助傳統啟發式方法的學習型解決方案。課程強調以實作為主，學生將以小組專題的方式，針對真實的 EDA 挑戰提出方法，例如 SAT 求解、技術映射、布局（placement），以及用於電路模擬的稀疏矩陣排序等問題。

課程內容包含：
機器學習基礎講授、領域專家介紹最先進的可在指數級搜尋空間中進行啟發式探索的 EDA 演算法，以及相關文獻的論文導讀。

課程的主要重點將放在小組專題。課堂中將安排專題提案、進度報告與期末成果發表等環節。
修課學生將能夠：
將 EDA 最佳化問題表述為機器學習任務，並選擇合適的方法與模型。
分析傳統啟發式演算法，找出可由學習方法取代或增強的決策點。
設計並實作適用於指數級組合搜尋空間之最佳化問題的強化學習方法。
評估學習型方法與傳統啟發式在解品質、計算成本與泛化能力等面向的權衡。
使用標準測資（ICCAD CAD Contest、ISPD、IWLS、SAT/QBF Competition）進行實驗評估。
批判性閱讀並分析近期機器學習與設計自動化交叉領域的研究文獻。
課程目標:
提供機器學習的理論基礎，並說明其在各類 EDA 主題中的適用性。
激發研究生階段的新研究方向：包含新的研究專題或現有專題的延伸方向。
讓學生熟悉機器學習的開發環境。
課程要求:
建議先修課程：
電子設計自動化導論、機器學習

評分方式： 課程參與（25%）、專題報告與成果（75%）
專題小組需於課堂上進行提案簡報、中期進度報告與期末成果發表。
此外，學生也需報告與其專題相關的論文評論。

課程概述:
1. 論文研讀 : 說明研究問題,文獻現有解決方法與其技術
2. 書報討論: 提出新想法,解決研究問題
3. 碩論進度報告: 電路說明, 電路模擬,電路佈局,量測考量
4. 其他事項討論
課程目標:
1. 訓練學生能了解研究問題,提出新想法與文獻現有解決方法加以比較
2. 完成晶片設計與量測
3. 發表論文

課程概述:
Composition II is a year-long course that focuses on writing full-length essays. In the previous semester, we closely examined four important writing skills: summarizing, evaluating, synthesizing, and arguing. These together set the core foundation for academic writing. In this semester, we will continue practicing these skills by going deeper into the “They say – I say” dialogue. A range of templates will be shared to help you formulate more complex sentences, which is essential for building nuanced, insightful, and contextually-sensitive arguments. Towards the end of the semester, we will also go through some forms of writing that many of you will encounter when applying for graduate school or short-term study abroad programs.

One additional area that we will be exploring this semester is the role of AI in academic writing. Specifically, we will be having several rounds of in-depth conversations on this topic, including: 1) how college students frequently use (and misuse) AI in writing, 2) what principles are usually highlighted in institutional AI policies, 3) in what ways can AI-assisted technologies be ethically incorporated into our writing, and finally 4) to what extent can human potential and human agency be enhanced – or undermined – in the process of working with AI.
課程目標:
By the end of this course you will:

•	Be more confident in engaging with – and responding to – different academic texts and debates
•	Advance your skills in summarizing, evaluating, synthesizing, and arguing

In the previous semester, we closely examined four important writing skills: summarizing, evaluating, synthesizing, and arguing. These together set the core foundation for academic writing. 課程概述:
This course explores the timeless journey of coming of age through a diverse selection of literary works, ranging from classic novels to contemporary fiction and short stories. By examining these texts, students will delve into the emotional, social, and cultural challenges faced by characters as they navigate the transition from youth to adulthood. Through close reading and class discussions, we will explore how themes like identity, relationships, societal expectations, and self-discovery are reflected and reimagined across different historical periods, cultural contexts, and narrative styles.

The course begins with two short stories—James Joyce’s “Araby” and Amy Tan’s “Rules of the Game”—which provide insights into the nuanced experiences of adolescence and early self-realization. We then move to a study of four novels: Sally Rooney’s Normal People, a contemporary exploration of complex relationships and emotional growth; Charlotte Bronte’s Jane Eyre, a classic narrative of resilience and self-definition within the constraints of Victorian society; Kazuo Ishiguro’s Never Let Me Go, a poignant reflection on identity and purpose within an unsettling dystopian world; and Ocean Vuong’s On Earth We’re Briefly Gorgeous, a poetic and deeply personal tale of memory, heritage, and becoming.

By engaging with these texts, students will develop critical reading and analytical skills while considering the universal and diverse aspects of growing up. Discussions will focus on how the coming-of-age experience is shaped by gender, class, culture, and historical context. Assignments will encourage students to connect the texts to their own experiences and the broader world around them, fostering both literary appreciation and personal reflection. 

* Non-major students interested in the course might need to wait until the semester begins to enroll, as they may not be able to register online.

**International students are welcome to join if they are interested in reading the assigned texts.

 If you have any questions, feel free to contact the instructor: brucehuang@ntu.edu.tw
課程目標:
1.	Develop Literary Analysis Skills: Students will develop essential skills for literary analysis and generate pertinent questions about the text, its contexts, and its implications, enabling them to approach other literary works independently.

2.	Familiarity with Major Themes: Students will become familiar with major themes and issues in coming-of-age narratives, such as identity formation, personal growth, societal expectations, and the complexities of relationships.

3.	Craft and Articulate Interpretations: Students will craft and articulate original interpretations of literature, supporting their arguments with solid evidence from the texts.

4.	Explore Cultural and Historical Contexts: Students will gain insights into how coming-of-age experiences are shaped by cultural, historical, and social factors, examining perspectives from diverse time periods, settings, and voices.

5.	Enhance Communication and Collaboration: Students will improve their critical thinking, written, and oral communication skills through participation in discussions, group activities, and storytelling projects. Collaborative assignments will also foster teamwork and peer engagement.
課程要求:
Discussion Questions: As part of the pre-class effort, each student should write two general questions (around 120 words each but no more than 150) about the reading of the week and submit them as an assignment on NTUCOOL (due Sunday at noon). The instructor will sort the questions and post those to be used for discussion in class the next day. Good questions will demonstrate the students’ deep engagement with the texts.

Participation: Students are required to come to class meetings prepared to discuss the assigned texts and actively participate in group discussions. Each group, consisting of 4-5 members, will provide in-depth answers to one of the week’s discussion questions. After class, students must fill out an online survey (via Google Forms, by Tuesday midnight) to rate the performance of each group member. 

Group Presentation: After discussion, each group will present its ideas for 5 minutes (and no more). A good presentation will have a concise central idea, supported by details from the texts. All members will receive the same presentation grade. Students should listen carefully to the presentations and mark fairly on the grading sheet.

Response Papers: Students will write three response papers (800–900 words each). The first paper must be on Normal People. Of the other three novels, submit papers on any two; if all three are submitted, the two highest scores will count. Each paper has its designated deadline; late submissions will not be accepted retroactively. Response papers should focus on a central issue or topic that is clearly connected to the course—such as themes discussed in class, questions raised in group work, or topics addressed in presentations. The aim is for students to engage deeply with the text in relation to the course content and to articulate their analysis of key themes and elements.

Story-Telling Project: For this project, students will work individually or in groups to create a story that relates to the course content and extends their understanding coming-of-age themes. The format is flexible and can include any medium, such as a video, podcast, creative writing piece, comics, or music. 

Project Exhibition: In the final class meeting, students will showcase their story-telling projects through a poster exhibition. Each group or individual will present their project, providing an opportunity for peers to engage with and appreciate the diverse ways in which coming-of-age can be interpreted and represented.

課程概述: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the theory, research, and practice of language teaching, establishing a methodological foundation for future language educators. It explores current foreign language teaching approaches, fundamental principles of language learning and teaching, and their application in diverse instructional contexts. Beyond theoretical understanding, the course equips prospective teachers with practical teaching strategies and techniques aligned with established pedagogical principles. Through interactive activities and hands-on teaching experiences, students will examine effective instructional methods and learning resources, fostering their teaching competencies and professional growth.
課程目標: 本課程提供語言教學理論、研究與實踐的全面介紹，為未來語言教育工作者奠定方法論基礎。課程內容涵蓋當前外語教學方法、語言學習與教學的核心原則， 以及其在多元教學情境中的應用。除理論理解之外，課程亦培養學生掌握符合既定教學原則的實用教學策略與技巧。透過互動式學習活動與實作教學經驗， 學生將探討有效的教學方法與學習資源，以提升其教學能力並促進專業成長。
課程要求:
1. Reading Reports and Class Discussion (閱讀報告與課堂討論)
Students will deliver brief team-based presentations on assigned textbook chapters and facilitate short discussions.

2. Micro-Teaching Demonstration (小組微型教學演示)
After one group presents a reading report that introduces key principles and techniques, another group will conduct a micro-teaching session lasting 20 to 25 minutes on the same topic.

3. Lesson Plan and Teaching Demonstration (教案設計與教學演示)
Each group will create a lesson plan and present a teaching demonstration lasting 20 to 30 minutes later in the semester.

4. Reflection on Learning (學習反思)
Students will be guided to reflect at the end of class on their reading, group discussions, or class activities. 

5. Self and Peer Evaluation (自評互評)
Students will evaluate their own teaching practices, as well as those of their peers, using the provided rubric.

6. Attendance and Class Participation (課堂參與)
Consistent attendance and active participation are vital for achieving success in this course. Arriving more than 30 minutes late or leaving early may be recorded as an absence. If you need to request time off, please notify the instructor and submit your leave request through the NTU Online Leave Request System. Please be aware that excessive unexcused absences can negatively impact your final grade.

課程概述:
本課程預計透過「樂動」；即「音樂的動態行動」之概念，探索台灣的近代社會。我們將試圖體會在這個島嶼上，歷史和當代的人們經由各種樂舞活動所創造的共同意義和其影響。我們的目標是透過仔細聆聽和樂動參與，對過去150年來塑造台灣的社會組織和變遷，產生反思性、身體性、與情感性的不同觀點與新理解。我們會接觸各式各樣的傳統與當代樂種，包括儀式樂舞、社群樂舞、具政治性的樂舞、與大眾流行音樂。然而我們不求定義「台灣音樂」是什麼，也不力圖全面認識所有在台灣的樂種；反之，我們將藉由不同議題的探索—包括社群凝聚、移民與人權、墾殖、殖民現代性、政治與經濟、族群身分、多元文化與原住民主權、性別與性向、空間與環境、社會運動等—嘗試理解住在這塊土地上的原住民、漢人、新住民、及訪客，如何透過不同類型的音樂和舞蹈發聲與行動。

＊本課程將以英語進行，通常有許多國際交換生修課，歡迎本地同學來修課交流，課程著重於課堂小組分組討論、分組報告及小組合作寫作。
＊第一階段未選上的同學歡迎來旁聽第一堂課。本課程採用第三類（線上系統自動）加選，不發放加簽碼。
課程目標:
1)	基礎認識台灣各族群的不同傳統與當代音樂(與舞蹈)

2)	透過聆聽、發聲、舞動、表演等媒介反思自己與台灣歷史和社會的關係和所在位置

3)	應用「樂動」的概念，理解音樂表演在社會中扮演的動態角色，並發展批判思考能力，以分析多樣樂種與塑造社群、身分認同、政治經濟、與社會運動之關係。
課程要求:
1.	聆聽討論：本課程不需要任何音樂知識背景。然而，學生需在課前閱讀或觀看指定文章或影片，並在課堂上積極參與小組的聆聽討論。
2.	反思寫作：學生需撰寫每週預備討論的短作業，並完成三篇反思日誌，以整合跨週模組中的所學內容。任何明顯由生成式AI撰寫且未標註出處的寫作，將依據AI檢測結果大幅扣分。
3.	小組閱讀報告：學生將隨機分組，於第六至十三週間報告

課程概述:
This course develops students’ academic English proficiency in the Social Sciences domain through a structured progression from academic writing to oral communication.

The first part of the course focuses on foundational academic writing skills necessary for producing a structured social science report. Students learn how to formulate clear thesis statements, distinguish claims from opinions, integrate academic sources, develop analytical paragraphs, construct policy recommendations, and revise for clarity and coherence. The midterm assessment requires students to submit an evidence-based written report.

The second part of the course emphasizes oral communication in academic and professional contexts. Students practice persuasive speaking, academic presentations, data explanation, networking, interviews, and group facilitation. The final assessment requires students to present their written report orally, demonstrating structured argumentation, confident delivery, and effective audience engagement.

Through a task-based and skills-oriented approach, the course prepares students to communicate ideas clearly, critically, and confidently in English across academic and professional social science settings.
課程目標:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

	Construct a structured academic report that presents a clear thesis, integrates relevant sources, develops coherent analysis, and offers reasoned recommendations.
	Apply essential academic writing skills, including summarizing and paraphrasing, citation integration, logical organization, and revision for clarity and precision.
	Deliver structured and persuasive oral presentations based on written academic work, demonstrating effective organization, delivery techniques, and audience awareness.
	Communicate professionally in academic and workplace contexts, including networking, interviews, team discussions, and persuasive exchanges.
	Demonstrate academic integrity and responsible use of AI tools in both written and oral assignments.

課程概述:
In this course, students will enhance their English proficiency and disciplinary literacy through the dynamic lens of agriculture and bioresource sciences. This course aims to equip students with the linguistic tools necessary for academic success in English-medium environments, particularly in fields related to agriculture and bioresources. By integrating content-based instruction with practical language applications, students will develop crucial skills in reading complex texts, engaging in scientific discourse, taking effective notes, and exercising critical thinking. This course is designed to foster not only language competence but also confidence in using English in their future academic and professional careers. Upon completion, students will be better prepared to tackle advanced studies and contribute to global discussions in their fields.

To achieve these goals, the course is structured around several thematic units, each designed to focus on specific integrated language skills tailored to contexts in agriculture and bioresources. These units will explore topics such as sustainable farming practices, food and society, and environmental impacts of agricultural development. Within each unit, students will practice and refine their reading comprehension through analysis of scientific articles, enhance their spoken English during class discussions and presentations, and develop their writing and note-taking skills by summarizing key information and arguments. This integrated approach ensures that students not only learn English in an applied manner but also gain a deep understanding of important issues facing the agricultural sector today, preparing them for real-life applications and further specialized studies.

Note: This course will be conducted entirely in English.

Upon completion of this course, students will be able to demonstrate the following Core Competencies (CC):

CC1: Advanced Vocabulary Acquisition
Mastery of specialized terminology and phrases pertinent to bioresources and agriculture.

CC2: Reading Comprehension
Ability to critically analyze and understand a variety of texts, including textbooks, popular writing, and scientific research, related to agriculture and bioresource sciences.

CC3: Oral Communication Skills
Proficiency in discussing and presenting on topics related to agriculture, engaging in academic discourse, and articulating arguments and insights in a clear, organized manner.

CC4: Writing and Note-Taking Proficiency
Skills in writing coherent, structured texts such as summaries and essays, as well as taking thorough and useful notes during lectures and from reading materials.

CC5: Critical Thinking and Analysis
Capacity to evaluate and synthesize information from various sources, critically assess arguments, and contribute thoughtfully to discussion on agricultural and bioresource issues.

CC6: Communicative and Team Skills
Ability to communicate effectively with team members in order to organize ideas and workflow.

課程概述:
本課程將介紹生物資訊學在日常生活中的應用。我們將探索DNA和基因的功能、人類基因組的定序及定序技術的進步。接著我們將了解DNA突變如何導致遺傳疾病，並進一步討論生物資訊學在個人化精準醫療和癌症治療中的應用。我們也將介紹液體活檢和產前檢測在檢測基因突變和疾病中的診斷潛力。此外，我們將討論生物資料庫和全基因組關聯研究（GWAS）在偵測致病基因中的應用，以及與臨床基因組數據的倫理及個人隱私相關問題。我們還將審視生物資訊分析如何揭示家族史及人類群體的遺傳多樣性。

在整個課程中，我們將透過觀看影片並進行小組討論，以加深對課程主題的理解。

課程概述:
Learn about Taiwan’s geology and how the island has formed on this four-day excursion to the beautiful Hengchun Peninsula in southern Taiwan. During the course, you will see million-years old rock formations, search for fossilized shells in the jungle, and explore the spectacular landscape of uplifted ancient coral reefs. On our way, we will stop at the earthquake museum in Wufeng, and we will also visit Moon World where you can explore a landscape that looks as if it were from another planet.
This course is designed for non-geology students, which gives a general geological introduction to Hengchun Peninsula, Southern Taiwan. Students will learn how to observe the field and take geological surveys to understand surface geology. This course includes one indoor class, one rock identification class, a four-day field excursion with daily assignments, and the final exam.
The field excursion involves some challenging physical activities, such as climbing sharp coral reefs and hiking through a gorge. If you are interested in learning about geology while getting sweaty and dirty in the process, then this course is perfect for you.

The course will be taught in English and is specially designed for international students.

課程概述: 本課程旨在教授人文地理學的基礎概念，尤其從文化地理學的理論視角，切入幾個重要的研究主題，涵蓋後殖民、性別、階級、自然與都市等。除了引導修課學生對人文地理學有初步認識之外，本課程亦試圖透過文獻研讀與討論，梳理文化地理學的發展歷程及其所介入的重要爭辯。在課程設計上共分四單元。首先從文化作為地理學的研究課題開始，介紹1980年代地理學的文化轉向，從中說明視覺研究的重要性。文化轉向不僅影響了地理學的方法論，更讓地理學重思構成地景的權力關係。接著引介的是有關權力關係的討論，包括後殖民、性別與階級等議題，例如日本時代所拍攝的紀錄片中所再現的台灣，或者早期百貨公司的性別政治等。第三單元則聚焦社會與自然之間的關係，將探討動物地理學以及生態觀光等相關研究。最後，都市是當前人類主要的活動地區，本課程將在第四單元中介紹「漫遊者」、縉紳化以及公共空間的政治，深入都市日常生活的肌理。
課程目標: 本課程將引導修課學生培養人文地理學的基本素養，目標有三。首先，認識文化地理學的發展脈絡，並理解其如何介入既有議題的討論；其次，理解文化、社會與自然如何作為地理學關切的重要議題；最後，學習以地理學的觀點批判性地檢視日常生活的現象。
課程要求:
1.平時課堂出席與參與 (15%)
2.小組報告 (25%)
3.期末考 (60%)

課程概述: 本課程屬於地理系大學部的地理資訊科學領域進階課程，先修科目應包括：統計學、程式設計、地圖學與地理資訊系統等相關課程。課程目的在於介紹空間資料分析方法、應用並深化資料分析的實作能力等，使其瞭解各種分析方法運用的時機、模式分析與報表解讀等，並補充實證研究論文的導讀，說明在空間分析研究上的實用性，提供地理系或相關系所同學能運用適當的空間分析方法，進行地理學相關議題的研究。本學期的授課主題包括：地理空間視覺化（geospatial visualization）、地理數據處理（geo-processing）、點型態分析（point pattern analysis）、空間自相關（spatial autocorrelation）、熱區分析（hot spot analysis）等；輔以導讀地理空間觀點的實證論文，理解各種方法的延伸應用。本課程將使用R程式及其空間分析套件，培養同學對於空間資料分析的實作能力。
課程目標: 本課程將介紹空間分析方法的理論觀念，將以統計學、程式設計、地圖學與地理資訊系統等相關課程為先修基礎，進一步從機率與推論統計的觀點，深化各種空間分析方法的理論基礎，提供同學進階的地理資訊分析能力。本課程將提供同學了解空間分析方法的基本觀念與理論，並透過各種領域的應用實例，瞭解空間分析作為一種跨學科應用的潛在可能。

課程概述:
區域地理（Regional Geography）為地理學的重要研究領域，概可分為「區域研究與地理 （regional studies and geography)」與「國際區域地理 (world regional geography)」兩大取徑。

前者強調發生在都市與區域空間下，人文、經濟、交通、聚落、政治等空間環境規劃議題；後者則是從帝國擴張、現代國家概念，到二戰之後的殖民地獨立與後殖民思潮等時間軸線，如何看待不同世界區域下之所謂國家內部與國際間發展差異，進而提供更整體且立體的地理空間觀點。

本課程以「國際區域地理」為設計核心，旨在介紹國際發展理論與其重要議題，包括：傳統主流發展觀、馬克思主義發展觀、反發展與後發展論、貧窮理論、發展倫理等；並延伸至若干與SDGs相關的實務操作與未來挑戰，如國際援助、債務、NGO、環境、貿易，以及美國變數及中國崛起等議題。

修課學生需選定一個「非OECD國家」作為研究對象，深入掌握上述理論脈絡，進一步蒐集並分析該國具體發生的相關新聞與政策辯論，透過案例與文本的對讀，建立批判性的理解與對話。
課程目標:
1. 認識發展理論關鍵概念。
2. 了解國際發展實務重要議題與未來挑戰。
3. 熟悉全球南方國家發展多重面向。
4. 學習全球北方援助國與新興援助國在國際發展作為。
5. 探索與 AI 共存下正向循環之教與學可能性。

課程概述: Have you ever wondered how to get the right Angel investment for your start-up idea or Series A/B fundings for a fast growing company? Or you have an admiration to become a Venture Capitalist that will discover and help grow the next Unicorn like Airb&b, Uber, Ant Financial, Robinhood etc? If so, the Global Entrepreneurial Finance: Venture Capital and Private Equity is an introductory course into the creative and mysterious world of the venture capital (VC) and private equity(PE) investments. This course will bring in the latest and most used VC/PE investment methodologies and practical tools from Silicon Valley, the heart of the global VC/PE industry.   “Entrepreneurship” is a popular focus of discussion among businesspeople, financiers, economists, and policymakers. At a macro level, economists and policymakers have increased their attention to entrepreneurial enterprise because of its importance to economic growth, the significance of entrepreneurial businesses in job creation, and the role of business owners in aggregate saving and wealth accumulation. Today on the demand side, many M.B.A. students want to start their own businesses or be part of emerging businesses, while on the supply side, other M.B.A.s are interested in participating directly in the growth of venture capital and private equity sector.   What, then, is “entrepreneurial finance”? The second term is easier to define. We know that Finance studies encompass valuation and the allocation of resources, risk, liquidity, and information. Indeed, topics in finance related to valuing cash flows, assessing the cost of capital, choosing among suppliers of funds, and aligning incentives for value maximization are at least as important for entrepreneurial firms as for more established firms. In particular, new and growing firms likely face “financing constraints” on growth and difficult decisions about financial contracting; while present-day financial decisions may have a profound influence on the available range of future options and choices.   Defining entrepreneurship is less straightforward. Consistent with many popular characterizations of entrepreneurs, the noted Harvard economist Joseph Schumpeter summarized an entrepreneur as follows:   “To act with confidence beyond the range of familiar beacons and to overcome that [social] resistance requires aptitudes that are present only in a small fraction of the population and that define the entrepreneurial type...” (Capitalism, Socialism, and Democracy, New York: Harper and Row, 1942, page 132.)   Actually studying entrepreneurship requires a narrower focus. The economic concept corresponding most to topics we discuss in this course as “entrepreneurial finance” was articulated by Chicago economist Frank Knight who argued that entrepreneurs must address problems of raising capital and bearing risk in addition to identifying and pursuing opportunity. [Frank H. Knight, Risk, Uncertainty, and Profit, New York: Houghton Mifflin, 1921.] Throughout the course, we will emphasize such financial management decisions of entrepreneurial firms.   We define an entrepreneur as the person who puts the pieces together, identifies the new opportunity and/or market imperfection, connects the dots, and brings about change. Entrepreneurship may take place in small start-ups as well as large established firms. The entrepreneur may be the inventor, the financier, the manager, or somebody else entirely.   The capital market for financing such entrepreneurs – and private equity investing more generally – differs fundamentally from capital markets considered in standard corporate finance: First, start-ups are young, mostly unprofitable companies, with short operating histories and little capital. Young firms face exceptionally high degrees of uncertainty, constraining financing and creating difficult decisions about financial contracting, keeping in mind that today’s financial decisions may have implications for future opportunities and choices. Second, capital markets for privately held companies are predominantly “deal markets” where terms and valuations are negotiated on a case-by-case basis, where investors can add value and are actively involved with the companies they finance. Throughout the course, we emphasize financial opportunities and decisions of entrepreneurs and private equity investors investing in these entrepreneurs.
課程目標: We will start with investigating the overall ecosystem and relationship between start-ups, VC’s, and Fund of Funds; then we will pick up the practical tools on the legal framework, organizational structures, funding channels and types, pre and post-money valuation methodologies, and pipeline generation. Later in the course we will deep dive into the exiting strategies including M&A, roadshow preparation, IPO, (Leveraged) Buyout, secondary market sales, and final LP/GP distributions. Throughout the course, students will be tracking the current start ups and VC/PE funding rounds as they happen and cross-reference these real life deals with the tools and methodologies delivered in this course.
課程要求: Basic understanding of managerial accounting and corporate finance is ideal but not a must; some experiences with start-ups would be a plus. A Keen interest in how private investment and alternative investment works in the context of macro and micro economics and capital market performances.

Financial Analysis: Ratio Analysis
Working Capital management/managing financial operations
Cost Management and Decision Making
Budgeting and Performance Management,
Reward System and Compensation

Risk and Capital Budgeting

Hospital accreditation is a worldwide trend to assure hospital quality and patient safety. Patient safety is also an important issue in health policy for most developed countries. This course will cover major topics for hospital accreditation and patient safety including the history, current status, and its impact on Taiwan and around the world as well as future perspective. The patient-focus method and Joint Commission International Accreditation (JCIA) will be covered.  Definition, classification, reporting system, tools, and measures in patient safety will be included, too.

2. Acquire both theoretical and practical knowledge of cross-cultural communication.

3. Cultivate competence in oral, written, and interpersonal communication and collaboration skills through the group project.

4. Develop a culture-sensitive perspective to understand the cultural differences in various contexts and address their challenges.

課程概述: Since the advent of Web 2.0 and online social networking, social media platforms, establishing and fostering general-purpose or interest-based communities that give their users the power to actively create and contribute user-generated contents and connect and interact with others, have exploded in popularity. As a result, social media has become one unique, novel source of big data, providing great opportunities and magnificent potential for research to analyze and understand human behavioral patterns or to develop advanced analytics techniques that analyze social media data for business decision support or more effective social media management. For example, individuals increasingly share on social media platforms their experiences with, preferences for, and opinions about a wide range of products, entities (e.g., organizations, celebrities, politicians), emerging events, public policies, and so on. Organizations increasingly rely on these user reviews to answer such questions as: What do customers say about us and about our competitors? What do they like or dislike about our products? What causes customers to become dissatisfied?
課程目標: Social media analytics (SMA) refers to “the process and methods of collecting and analyzing data gathered from social media channels to support business decisions.” The objective of this course is to help students understand commonly discussed topics and their corresponding analytics methods related to social media analytics. This course is structured into three modules: SMA essentials, network-based SMA methods, and text-based SMA methods. Technically speaking, social media analytics is a confluence of research in data mining, text mining, and social network analysis. Thus, in the “SMA essentials” module, we will cover these fundamental building blocks of social media analytics, including 1) data mining essentials, 2) text mining essentials, and 3) social network analysis and link prediction. The “network-based SMA methods” module will cover the topics that heavily rely on the structural analysis of social networks to support the analysis of social media. They include 1) community detection, 2) influence modeling, and 3) opinion leader detection. In the “text- based SMA methods” module, we will discuss the methods and applications that predominantly exploit the texts (user-generated contents) shared on social media platforms. They include 1) sentiment analysis, 2) social media for marketing intelligence, 3) user profiling, and 4) fake review detection.

課程概述:
商業模式 (Business Model) 是企業創造、傳遞及獲取價值的核心邏輯。透過系統性地解構商業模式的關鍵要素，企業得以清楚界定自身的市場定位與競爭策略，進而實現可持續的價值創造。自1990年代末期電子商務興起以來，資訊科技持續驅動商業模式的演進，並在行動網路時代催生了AirBnB、Uber等共享經濟代表性企業，深刻改變既有產業結構。
隨著生成式AI (Generative AI) 的爆發性發展，我們正處於新一波產業革命的浪潮。本課程將透過經典與前沿的新創案例，探討資訊科技如何推動商業模式創新；除分析過往成功的平台與數位經濟模式外，本學期亦將新增「生成式AI」單元，深入探討企業如何運用 AI 重塑價值鏈、改變內容生產與服務提供方式，並創造全新的使用者互動與商業模式。
在案例分析過程中，我們將剖析資訊科技如何帶來新的價值主張、計價收費機制、服務設計與通路模式。然而，我們必須提醒創新者：多數商業模式是可以模仿的，除非擁有難以複製的競爭優勢（如Google的關鍵字廣告結合其強大的搜尋引擎技術），否則創新只能帶來短暫的領先。本課程的核心目標，即在於引導學員思考如何從這短暫的優勢中建構競爭壁壘，有效防禦後進者的威脅。

A business model is the core logic through which a firm creates, delivers, and captures value. By systematically deconstructing the key elements of a business model, firms can clearly define their market positioning and competitive strategy, thereby achieving sustainable value creation. Since the rise of e-commerce in the late 1990s, information technology has continuously driven the evolution of business models. In the era of mobile networks, it has given rise to emblematic sharing-economy companies such as Airbnb and Uber, profoundly reshaping existing industry structures.
With the explosive development of generative AI, we are now entering a new wave of industrial transformation. Through both classic and cutting-edge startup cases, this course examines how information technology drives business model innovation. In addition to analyzing successful platform and digital-economy models from the past, the course introduces a dedicated Generative AI module this semester. This module explores how firms leverage AI to reconfigure value chains, transform content production and service delivery, and create entirely new forms of user interaction and business models.
Throughout the case analyses, we will dissect how information technology enables new value propositions, pricing and revenue mechanisms, service designs, and distribution channels. At the same time, innovators must be reminded that most business models are inherently imitable. Unless a firm possesses hard-to-replicate competitive advantages—such as Google’s keyword advertising integrated with its powerful search engine technology—innovation typically delivers only temporary leadership. The core objective of this course is therefore to guide participants in thinking about how to build durable competitive moats from such transient advantages and effectively defend against latecomers.

4. Explore different methods for doing research and work around HCI.

5. Make connections between HCI and the disciplines it commonly draws from, including but not limited to psychology, computer science, information science, and anthropology.

6. Get experience in conducting interdisciplinary and group research in HCI.

你是不是很好奇，市面上的軟體都是如何開發出來的？
你是不是有很多的想法，但是卻不知道該如何實踐？
你開發了一個網路應用服務，但是不知道如何可以給更多人使用？

課程概述:
使學生能了解刑法分則各個法益與條文內容之關連性。課程教學主軸，不僅期望學生能夠習慣刑法高度抽象與邏輯性的犯罪審查過程，還必須深切地體悟刑罰之施與是一種高度的國家強制行為，在個案犯罪刑事責任的判定過程中，必須嚴守最後手段性與罪刑法定主義的基本要求，以求將刑罰的施用範疇壓抑至最低，以期學生於在學期間，培養我國刑法犯罪成立與刑罰制度的基礎觀念，養成足夠的批判能力，對我國現行刑法理論與立法動向進行反省與思考，將來進入實務工作後，也能夠謹慎地運用刑法的論理與解釋方法，能夠在未來應對實務個案時，有效且合理地限制刑罰。

課程概述:
本學期課程以「公法學及其方法論之深層結構」為核心問題意識，嘗試將公法方法論理解為一套嵌入於法治國權力配置之中的制度性語言，而非中立的解釋或適用技術。課程以德國公法學的歷史發展為主要分析脈絡，探討在不同法治國型態下，立法、行政與司法三者之間的權力分工，如何透過公法方法論被具體化、穩定化，並在制度條件變遷時產生張力與轉移。

課程內容將自德意志帝制時期與威瑪共和的法學發展出發，延伸至基本法時期的憲法實踐，分析議會保留、比例原則、行政判斷餘地、程序化與司法審查密度等核心方法論概念，如何回應立法能力、行政專業化與司法角色擴張等制度現實。課程特別著重於「價值決定權」與「事後評價權」之區分與互動，並以此作為理解公法學內部權力結構的重要分析工具，並用以反思我國處境與面臨之共同問題。

課程亦將與同學報告主題分工，探討民主法治國當前所面臨的關鍵難題，包括立法空洞化、行政負載過重、法院擴權，以及刑事程序、風險治理等高度張力領域中所浮現的制度極限。本課程希望引領同學對公法學之結構性理解能力，使修課同學能辨識公法方法論何以在特定制度前提下運作，又何以在前提動搖時承受過度負載，進而引發法治國內部的緊張與調整。
課程目標:
修課同學應能透過此課程，掌握以下知識與思辯能力：
1. 藉助德國法學發展史，理解公法方法論背後所預設的權力結構
2. 認識立法、行政、法院在不同法治國型態中的角色轉變
3.分析「價值決定權」與「事後評價權」之法學權力分配與制衡關係
4. 批判性思考民主法治國家法律失靈、行政失能與法院擴權之危機與轉機
課程要求: 修課同學應積極參與課程主題之學習與思考，並選定我國制度運作相關問題提出口頭與書面報告

課程概述:
冤案於古今中外之人類社會皆為相當受矚目之議題，近年因蘇建和案、徐自強案、邱和順案、鄭性澤案及江國慶案等案件，使台灣社會逐漸開始關注冤案。透過冤案檢視刑事司法程序中的錯誤，並透過重回訴訟程序的實際模擬，是避免錯誤及增進刑事辯護策略與技術的最好方法。

課程概述:
動物學是一門探討生命現象中著重於動物領域的科學，必須藉實驗課程將正課介紹的觀念具體化，使學生由親自動手操作的過程中，學習動物學的基本實驗技術、印證生命科學的基本理論，更重要的是從中體會科學研究的方法與精神。
實驗課程以本系所編寫之「普通動物學實驗指導」為講義，講義皆由本系多位教授共同編寫，總共規畫有近三十個實驗，涵括動物學的重要領域。如細胞與組織、器官和各系統的結構與作用、動物的生理機制、生命的延續、動物的分類及演化、動物的行為以及生態等。本課程以此講義為依據，先以講演的方式，配合投影片和短片，將每一實驗所根據之基本理論及實驗內容，作具體而微、深入淺出的介紹。繼而令修習之學生親手操作，完成該實驗並討論之。
課程目標:
期望藉由本實驗課程的訓練，使學生對動物學有一基礎認知，並擁有動物學的基本實驗技術以及正確且良好的生物實驗態度，同時藉由多樣的實驗引發學生對生命科學的興趣。
修習本課程後，學生應：
1. 能正確辨別動物從細胞到器官的各個層級的生理構造，並了解其功能及特徵。
2. 能辨識不同種類的動物，並了解其生理特徵或功能的差異。
3. 具備能正確使用顯微鏡、解剖用具、微量吸管等生物實驗器材的能力。
課程要求: 學生必須事先預習該次實驗之內容，上課時必須實際親自動手操作，按時完成實驗後的報告、作業或科學繪圖。

課程概述: 保育植物多樣性是台灣自然資源永續發展的重大議題。本課程藉由學生暑假密集在辜嚴倬雲植物保種中心，與蒐藏經理實地參與熱帶植物異地活體保存策略；並透過實習期間植物溫室植物換盆栽培實作，了解物種之經營管理方針。台灣位居亞熱帶及熱帶交界，加上地形變化大，生態棲位豐富、植物相特有種比例極高。在現今人為活動大量干擾森林生態系完整性的情況下，保育熱帶植物遂成為刻不容緩的議題。位於屏東縣高樹鄉的保種中心，已成功復育出3萬4千種來自世界各地的熱帶植物，是台灣最大的熱帶活體植物收藏與研究中心，也是亞洲規模第一。學生參與此課程將可實際參與保育重要熱帶植物，獲得熱帶植物主要分類群認識鑑定能力、練習照料植物之栽培管理、觀察比較不同熱帶植物生長環境異同及參與原生物種保育計畫。修課學生未來將能實際應用這些方法、技術及觀念，投入業界植物栽培技術研發或應用於物種保育研究課題。
課程目標: 1.修課學生將可藉此課程實際訓練植物栽培技術，學生將習得世界各大重要熱帶植物如蘭科、鳳梨科、天南星科、薑科、芭蕉科、赫蕉科、棕櫚科、竹芋科、苦苣苔科、芸香科、秋海棠科、山茶科、蘚苔及蕨類。針對物種分類、多樣性、栽培生長型及人工繁殖策略，親身體驗了解熱帶植物保種復育的策略與作法。 2.本學科所得之實做知識可應用於植物園經營，原生物種保育、園藝育種及生技業界溫室管理，提供學生未來職涯規劃經驗。其實務經驗並可延伸至參與公職考試中生物多樣性及保育生物學學門。
課程要求: 由於保種中心住宿空間有限，欲修課同學需先繳交一份見習計畫書給老師同意後再選課(leafy@ntu.edu.tw)，內容包括：個人簡歷、相關修課經歷、申請緣由、欲學習之類群。 為了讓同學能夠實地體驗植物保種工作，本課程於暑假期間（七月份大約四周)，住宿屏東辜嚴倬雲植物保種中心密集上課，獲亦可選擇所參訪的政府或民間機構實習。第1週為該中心蒐藏之熱帶植物類群概述及蒐藏現況課程，之後由同學選取有興趣的植物類別，進行1週見習課程。見習課程將包含植物辨認、植物栽培及照護、溫室管理維護等課程。並且可與蒐藏經理做研究專題，見習課程結束前須報告專題或見習成果。學生修課評量原則上也包含見習操作與專題報告(口頭+文字)。 評分方式以學期中三、四次上課老師介紹重要植物類群特徵，學生上台報告自己興趣類群的期刊文章保育策略。 保種中心提供宿舍，並有可供學員自行料理之膳食廚房。

課程概述: Business today is by all measures -- global. No business or industry of any size is immune from the global environment. Understanding the global economy, therefore, is important for all people engaged in business regardless of the size or type of business. This course will consist of the basic areas of global market management. The course explores the interrelation of government and business across borders and the economic dynamics between countries/regions, including a general overview of global business environment, foreign direct investment and entry strategies. The class will also discuss the management of global market and review several cases studies that epitomize the issues involved in today’s global world. In general, the major topics of global business will be discussed to give students a basic level of knowledge and skills involved in today’s global business environment. This is an introductory course about global market management and, therefore, a significant portion of the class will be taught through lectures, but we also will include guest speakers, video clips, class discussion and readings on current issues. The students, therefore, must keep up with readings and participate to the extent able with general discussions on the theories and material presented in class.待補
課程目標:
1. To give students the knowledge and understanding of the unique aspects involved doing 
     business internationally on a business, legal and political level.

2. To understand strategies used by business in the international market on a
      competitive basis.

3. To understand the cultural effect on business and to analyze the ethics involved in cross border 
     transactions 

4. To learn and apply skills learned in the class to current on-going issues involved in today’s global 
      market.

5. The students will learn the issues involved in entering foreign markets, global
      production and outsourcing as well as logistics and supply chain issues.

6. To understand the issues involved in developing economies and the business
     and political issues surrounding the business and market dynamics.

7. Most importantly, the students hopefully will create a general awareness of global issues that 
     will allow them deeper insight in world issues and will allow them to keep on top of issues that 
     may affect them as individuals and as part of a larger entity.

課程概述:
十二年國教自然科學領域課程重視並貫徹「探究與實作」的精神與方法，尤其強調跨學科領域的整合與運用。本課程依據該理念，以培養師資生具備自然科學跨學科領域探究與實作之教學知能及課程發展素養。除師資生外，本課程亦適合非師資生之大學部學生和研究生修習，以建立自然科學跨學科領域合作的基本素養，符合現今科學研究趨勢。
課程由董桂書副教授主授，搭配臺北市立建國高級中學生物科劉翠華教師合授，並由國教署探究與實作推動中心(北區)教師團隊或其他科別的優秀高中教師支援。董桂書老師具20年師資培育課程教學經驗，帶過的師資生目前擔任國、高中專任教師的超過30位，個人曾3度榮獲校教學傑出獎。劉翠華老師為國立臺灣師範大學科學教育博士，曾獲教育部師鐸獎，擔任過臺北市教育局課程督學、國教署探究與實作研究教師，是高中課程發展與設計的專家。
本課程之內容規劃分為二部分，理論及實務並重、並行，相互驗證。
第一部分，引導修課學生理解探究與實作的內涵，內容包括：自然科學的本質和研究方法、探究與實作課程的理論架構、探究與實作的課程設計，並觀摩各科或跨科探究與實作課程的實施和教學。
第二部分，透過自然科學領域的探究與實作的體驗活動與科學探究歷程的理論相互驗證。修課學生將分組，各組成員合作對探究與實作之課程發展、教學與評量等進行設計與實作，並辦理成果發表進行交流討論。
課程目標:
1. 提升修課學生對自然科學探究與實作的素養。
2. 理解十二年國教中對自然科學探究與實作的理念與學習重點。
3. 提升統整跨領域知識之能力，培養溝通表達技巧與團隊合作精神。
4. 培養探究與實作之教學設計及課程發展能力。
5. 增進反思和分析探究與實作課程及跨領域議題之能力。
6. 培養社會關懷和守護自然之價值觀與行動力。

5. 探討壓力、疾病與健康之關聯和預防
6. 增進學生關懷社會的能力
7. 實踐自殺防治推廣並宣導守門人之重要性

課程概述: 本課程以「社會參與」為主軸，系統性介紹防災理論與名詞、國際趨勢（如仙台架構、SDGs）、多國防災體系（台灣、日本、美國、印尼），以及台灣重大災害案例（921地震、莫拉克颱風、2024花蓮地震、馬太鞍堰塞湖）。課程並探討防災科技（如地震速報、公共警報系統、遙測與大數據）、NGO/NPO 的角色與協作模式，最後回到台灣對區域防災的貢獻與治理啟示。採案例分析、專題簡報與情境演練，累積跨域治理與韌性治理的實作能力。
課程目標:
修課完成後，學生將能：
1.說明防災理論、名詞與全球趨勢；
2.比較台、日、美、印尼之防災治理體系與運作；
3.解析台灣重大災害事件的風險成因、應變作為與復原治理；
4.評估防災科技在監測、預警與決策支援中的角色與限制；
5.說明 NGO/NPO 在備災、應變與復原各階段之功能與協作；
6.擬定具體的「區域合作與社會參與」導向之政策建議。

課程概述:
本課程旨在向學生介紹一系列可用於全球衛生領域相關的處理數據處理的實用工具。 學習本課程不需要具備任何數據處理經驗，我們將從基礎開始。本課程分為三個部分，涵蓋數據搜集過程、基礎數據清理和操作，最終將數據視覺化。

(1)	REDCap數據採集：這部分課程將介紹REDCap的使用。REDCap是一被國際研究界廣泛使用的電子數據採集（EDC）工具。課程將會講解如何建立一個REDCap project、設計數據收集工具、REDCap 中的數據管理功能、測試工具、最後實際使用手機或平板進行數據。課程中會穿插練習時間，為學生提供實踐經驗。

(2)	R 中的數據清理和操作：這部分課程旨在介紹 R軟體在數據整理上的應用。修習本課程不需要編碼方面的知識。我們將從 R 中的基本功能和概念開始介紹。學生將學習閱讀、清理和操作數據集的基礎知識。課程中，我們將討論常見的雜亂數據類型以及整理它們的方法。課程中會穿插編寫 R 代碼和準備分析數據的小練習。

(3)	數據視覺化：本節將介紹數據視覺話的原理和各種方法，以及構建有效且引人注目的視覺效果的關鍵步驟。學生將學習如何將數據轉化為各種受眾易於理解的信息。我們將介紹一些學生可以用於數據可視化目的的工具/資源。

課程概述:
Identity is the most significant driving force transforming ourselves, our homes, our communities, our networks, our societies, our globe, and our meta-realities. In this class, we embark on an individual-group journey to evolve our sustainable placemaking identity. Sustainability is the most pressing concept we must integrate into our personal values to facilitate resource conservation for future generations. Identity and sustainability are deeply rooted in our ecological and cultural systems; as actors, we must take localized action to materialize them.

In this context, we conceptualize landscape identity as our interpretation of our connection to the environments we inhabit. This concept is pivotal in landscape studies, influencing our everyday interactions. Historically, civilizations evolved alongside natural landscapes, yet the 20th century introduced a "new vernacular landscape" of suburban and industrial man-made elements, as noted by J.B. Jackson in A Sense of Place, A Sense of Time.

As we navigate the 21st century—marked by global warming, biodiversity loss, and technological acceleration—our relationship with the planet has become paramount. To foster a landscape identity rooted in planetary consciousness, we will utilize Global Regional Eco-Friendly Certifications (Labels) as a critical lens. These labels—ranging from the Satoyama Initiative to Rainforest Alliance and Cradle to Cradle—serve as institutionalized identities that define how regions and industries commit to the Earth.

Course Structure
This course unfolds in three transformative stages:

Phase I: Energy & Global Vision An introduction to landscape identity and the "energy" of place. We will research Global Eco-Labels to understand how different cultures codify their ecological values into recognizable standards.

Phase II: Satoyama Preservation & Self-Awareness
A deep dive into personal lifestyles and the ethics of co-habitation. We will analyze how regional eco-certifications—specifically those rooted in the Satoyama Initiative and Biodiversity Labels—influence our identity as "stewards" rather than just "consumers." 

Phase III: Talent Mobility, Urban-Rural Dynamics & Local Practice Exploring the synergy between urban energy and rural resilience. We will focus on Regional Eco-Labels in the context of the tea industry, examining how local certification can empower community identity and sustainable talent mobility.

The Final Synthesis
The course culminates in “The Future Dialogue: The Future I Talk to Today’s I.” Participants will envision the decade from 2044 to 2054, engaging in a dialogue between their future selves and their present selves, reflecting on how the ecological identities and certifications adopted today have shaped the world of tomorrow.

Remark: 
We will plan fieldtrips to Pinglin teatown and maybe to Chiayi BuDai wetland.
課程目標:
1. Reconstruct Landscape Identity through Planetary Consciousness
2. Analyze and Apply Global Eco-Friendly Certifications
3. Quantify Personal Impact and Ethical Consumption
4. Engage in Sustainable Placemaking & Regional Revitalization5. Speculative Design and Future Dialogue

This course is an academic writing and communication course designed for graduate students in the biodiversity sciences. It aims to cultivate rigorous scientific thinking while equipping students with the conceptual and practical skills required to communicate biodiversity research effectively to academic, professional, and societal audiences. Therefore, this course emphasizes training students to communicate effectively in the biodiversity sciences.

Students will receive systematic training in the structure and conventions of scholarly writing, including the IMRAD format, argument development, citation and referencing standards, and effective data visualization for scientific publications. More specifically, the course emphasizes reading, interpreting, and translating peer-reviewed articles, as well as adapting scientific messages to different audiences and contexts without compromising analytical rigor. Student evaluation will be based on oral presentations, class participation, and written assignments that reflect both conceptual understanding and academic writing competence.

課程概述:
This course will introduce modern computational methods for materials science, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) and density functional theory (DFT). Both AI/ML and DFT are becoming standard tools in chemistry, physics, and materials science. Deep learning specifically involves linking input data (features) with output data (labels) through a neural network. Neural networks are capable of approximating any function. A typical example is the relationship between a material's structure and its properties. Conversely, DFT is a computational method used to analyze the electronic structure of atoms, molecules, and materials. It is based on quantum mechanics and provides valuable insights into the properties and behavior of various materials. Both DFT and AI/ML have their own strengths and applications, and they can be combined. Depending on the engineering field and the specific problem, these methods can be relevant. Therefore, AI/ML and DFT are valuable tools for students who will become engineers and scientists.

Weekly Topics:
1	Introduce Python and install the computing environment.
2	Math review: Tensors and shapes
3	Introduction to machine learning (ML)
4	ML concepts: Regression, model assessment, classification, and kernel learning
5	Introduction to deep learning
6	Graph neural networks (GNN)
7	Equivariant neural networks
8	Mid-semester examination
9	Introduction to material science
10	Application of ML in material science
11	Introduction to density functional density (DFT) and Quantum ESPRESSO (QE)
12	Practical DFT with QE: Basic parameters
13	Practical DFT with QE: Advanced topics
14	Practical DFT with QE: Input generator
15	Combine DFT and ML
16	Final examination

Assessments:
* Mid-semester examination (50%): 3 hours
* Final examination (50%): 3 hours
課程目標:
1)Understanding the DFT and AI/ML concepts.
2)Can practice the DFT and AI/ML by using the open-source Quantum ESPRESSO, TensorFlow, and Pytorch.
3)Using the dataset from the Material Project.
Apply DFT and AL/ML for practical applications in material science, such as screening solar cell materials.

課程概述: 傳統科技與政治之關係一方面聚焦在如何利用科學幫助公共政策的型構及執行，另一方面則關注如何透過特定政策促進科學發展。不過，本課程跳脫以上科學工具論及政府研發政策的「科學與政治間彼此分離」角度，而試圖分析及探索科技及政治之間更深層的相互型塑關係。本課程將先藉由深度閱讀若干政治社會學及科技研究的經典為起點，接著在幾個重要議題：如國族主義的建構、種族與族群的爭議、新興的社會運動（環境及醫療）、科技民主及政經制度的重構等，探討當代科技與政治之間的繁複關係。
課程目標: 熟悉科技與政治相關理論，並藉理論基礎延伸到科技政策相關實務議題，企圖同時培養學生理論深度、應用理論、及創新理論與實務的能力。本課程以科學及科技作為主要探索領域，希望幫助學生學習及實踐國際性、多樣性及跨領域性的研究途徑。此外，本課程應有助學生未來多元地探索台灣本土有關科技的政治社會性之政策議題。
課程要求: 課程參與及討論、心得報告、期末報告

課程概述: 科技與性別的關係，逐漸在科技與社會研究（STS）領域中受到重視，其所關注面向包括女性如何參與科技發展，科技如何影響性別的角色及關係等。本課程將以法律與管制為切入點，透過檢視資訊與健康科技的諸多法律議題，觀察性別與科技間的互動，並且試圖對於背後的權力結構進行探究。
課程目標:
本課程在促進學生對下列議題的認識及思考：
1. 性別與科技如何相互形塑；
2. 重要的科技法律議題；
3. 從性別與科技的觀點檢視法律與管制。
課程要求: 閱讀指定文獻、準備課堂報告。於期末時提出符合學術撰寫格式且學術貢獻之報告。

課程概述: This syllabus is designed for a mini course for undergraduate and M.A. students. Over the course of the 8 sessions (two per day, once a week), students will investigate the international political economy of the People’s Republic of China. Once an exporter of socialist revolution and foreign aid during the Mao era, China is now a leading global power in trade, investment, and development finance. In this process of transformation, China is blurring boundaries between the state and business, challenging conventional ideas about development, and remaking international economic institutions. Topics covered include China’s trade, investment, development finance, participation in international institutions like the World Trade Organization and World Bank, and campaigns like the Belt and Road Initiative. The course will discuss the economics, politics, and ideas shaping China’s policy decisions, and critically consider their implications from the perspectives of domestic and international actors.

•Critically analyze key contemporary issues in China’s international political economy  
•Strengthen academic research and writing skills

課程概述:
內外科護理學分為一及二兩個獨立但相關之課程，整體目的為探討罹患疾病之成人，如何經歷健康─疾病之轉換階段，以及其住院期間之身心靈以及社會問題；漸進式重點如下：內外一著重於加強、整合並延續學生之基礎護理知識與技能，強調促進學生對成人各科之專業知識之了解與實際應用。此階段結束時，學生應(1)熟悉且能執行專業科別之照護重點及技術、(2)理解相關檢查及治療之意義、(3)識別病家之需求並設計及執行相對應之計畫。
護理的核心不僅在病人本身，亦在病人如何與醫護人員互動及建立關。因此，除延續內外一之重點，內外二進一步鼓勵學生反思自身之護理經驗、檢視醫護病關係、探討社會文化對病家之影響。此階段完成時，學生應(1)整合自身經驗，將自己之獨特思考融入專業照護、(2)對醫護病關係及社會文化問題具敏感度，可根據觀察到之狀況獨立執行以病人為中心之全人照護。
課程目標:
本學科的詳細目的有四：
1.	準備自己以了解病人(the preparation of the nurse for coming to know the other)：
a.	了解各科照護重點及護理技術
b.	了解健康─疾病轉換之要素與現象(change triggers)，如疾病種類、症狀表徵與其學理背景
2.	透過溝通、設身處地得了解病人(the nurse knowing the other intuitively)：
a.	建立溝通管道與治療性人際關係
b.	探索此疾病狀態對病家造成之需求影響(properties or patient call)，包括身心靈社會多方面之護理問題
3.	蒐集科學資料並做出判斷(the nurse knowing the other scientifically)：
a.	判讀相關檢驗報告
b.	執行護理評估
c.	熟悉找尋科學證據之資源與方式
d.	歸納護理問題及判斷其輕重緩急
4.	整合所學並歸納出對病人及專業的系統性知識(the nurse complimentarily synthesizing known others)：
a.	熟練執行護理技術
b.	規劃護理計畫(intervention or nurse response)
課程要求:
上課及臨床實習合計共8週，課室暨實習總行事曆請見附件一。
1. 內外科護理學(二)：3學分，約48小時，上課內容及時間請見附件二。
2. 內外科護理學實習(二)：3學分，總時數120小時，見習及實習內容與分組請見附件三。

課程概述:
Course description: this course is designed to provide the student with a solid foundation in ecological concepts, techniques and experimental design in field research as applied to coral reef ecosystems. It consists in one-week field based research at a marine research station around Taiwan. To have attended Ocean 5097 is strongly recommended for joining this course. Alternatively, solid knowledge on coral reefs and the environmental challenges they are currently facing is requested. The course will begin with a general introduction of the coral reefs and how they are influenced by global and local factors. It will quickly narrow down to the context of Taiwan by introducing the local context: known diversity, past disturbances, and current research. The major reef biota will be discussed in terms of their ecological requirements, roles on the reef and overall impact. Methods in ecological monitoring and sampling will be discussed and examined directly on the field and will serve as a baseline for a future long-term ecological assessment. Data analysis will consist in examining and comparing structure of benthic assemblages among sites and depths (basic knowledge on R software is recommended). Students are asked to provide a final report and a poster (electronic format) of their work a maximum one month after the last day on the field. 


Additional information: a pre-course discussion on preparation for the field trip (?3 hr) will be arranged early in the semester. Field course: during spring break week from April 2nd, 2017 (Monday) to April 6th, 2017 (Friday). Working hours: daily 9H00 – 17H00. Daily schedule (subject to changes):  theoretical class in the morning and field preparation (9H00 – 12H00), field work in early afternoon (13H00-15H00) and sample (pictures) / data analysis in late afternoon (15H00-17H00).
There is a quota of 6 students for this course. This is an advanced course on coral reef ecology and students without a strong biological/ecological background will not be considered. Students will not be able to enroll in the course until they contacted the instructor of the course, and have been notified that their application has been approved. All hours are conducted at field station (Green Island Marine Research Station, Academia Sinica) with the exception of a few hours of pre-course discussion for the preparation for the field trip, and the final written assessment (research project report and poster) are written up, designed, and submitted after departing the marine station (one month maximum).
Students are asked to subscribe for individual insurance. Students will need to make their own way to and from the marine station, as well as to cover their living expense. This is a class on ecology, and students will be asked to reduce their carbon footprint when residing at the station. 
Students are invited to bring their personal computer. All enrolled students MUST know how to swim, and to be comfortable in staying in the water (sea) for a prolonged period of time. Snorkeling is a central part of this course, and all students are encouraged to participate (also snorkeling skills will be tested individually before joining field work); wetsuits and snorkeling gear are available for hire at a small charge from diving shop. Diving certification is not necessary; however, certified divers may have the priority for this class and be involved in deeper surveys (possibly at higher cost to cover rental of diving gear).
Approximate costs for your reference (tentative location Green Island): Return ticket train Taipei – Taitung (1,566 NT$), return ticket boat Taitung – Ludao (920 NT$), daily expense for food (400 NT$), 5-days basic insurance (233 NT$). Total: 3,119 NT$ + possible cost of diving equipment. In addition, students are strongly recommended to rent electric motorbikes for moving on the island. 
Further details will be available to enrolled students early in semester 2. 
For enrollment or any questions related to this course, please contact the instructor: Dr Vianney DENIS, vianney.denis@gmail.com.
課程目標:
By the end of this course, students are expected to be able to:
1)	Conceive, design and implement field monitoring in research on coral reefs
2)	Describe, analyze and compare benthic community structure among locations and depths
3)	Introduce background of research, present the methodology, highlight results, and discuss main findings and their implications.
課程要求:
Participation and motivation on the field: 50 %
Final report and poster (to send a maximum one month after return): 50%

The report should include title, abstract, introduction, methods, results and discussion. The scientific poster will summarize content of the report – different example will be provided during the course.

課程概述:
近來健康照護專業發展趨勢逐漸由醫療模式走向社會模式，強調社會參與之健康概念。本課程的目標為培養職能治療學生具備於社區與長期照護情境提供服務的知能。
    課程內容將包含介紹社區介入之理論基礎，公共衛生觀點的社區發展理念，法規與制度，社區服務方案的模式發展、評估與執行等，並介紹常見之職能治療社區服務，包含三大主題：1) 活躍老化主題：社區老人健康促進與生活型態再造、跌倒預防、高齡友善社區營造；2) 長期照護議題：包含居家職能治療服務、失智症照護、日間照護等；3) 身心障礙者生活自立議題：低視能、科技與環境介入、社區精神復健、弱勢兒童與青少年者議題等。

3.	認識長期照顧、老人福利、身心障礙者權益保護、健康促進等相關法規制度
4.	瞭解職能治療於社區場域之功能與角色

本實習課程在提供大四學生對急性期及復健期之生理障礙病患之臨床實習機會。急性期之病患來自神經內外科、內科、骨科、整形外科、燒傷科之成人患者為主。內科及神經內外科之病患以腦血管病變，中樞神經系統病變、腦腫瘤、頭部外傷、脊髓損傷為主。職能治療除提供疾病早期之處理，如預防關節僵硬、皮膚傷害、肌力退化、及一般神經肌肉、知覺認知、日常生活等訓練外，亦需擔任教育及諮詢病人的角色。骨科及整形外科之病患以手部外傷、骨折固定、人工關節置換及截肢手術後的患者為主。職能治療以手術後的副木製作及肢體訓練為主。燒傷科病患之職能治療則以製作副木、維持關節活動度等治療項目為主，此部份之實習以床邊治療方式進行之。

復健期之病患來自復健病房及復健部門診之成人病患。病人診斷以腦血管病變、腦傷、脊髓損傷病患為主，時有神經肌肉病變、肌肉骨骼系統問題、退化性疾病、截肢、手部外傷、關節炎.......等病患。職能治療根據本專業之哲學與治療精神提供病患完整的服務，由神經肌肉感覺知覺認知心理社會日常生活能力、到工作能力之加強，藉由個別治療及團體治療的方式達成。此部份之實習以在西址職能治療室進行治療。

所有學生皆需至東、西址之職能治療實習，由此可經驗不同診斷的病人，病患於不同時期職能治療的治療重點，及完整的治療程序，由接案之評估到病患將出院之輔具建議及相關準備工作。臨床之指導老師大多為資深之臨床治療師，學系之老師亦兼任醫院臨床工作及指導實習，各有專精，使學生更能將所學之理論做實際的運用。在十二週之實習過程中，除在指導老師的監督下實施評估治療病人外，每週亦安排有相關的演講、病人討論會及學生作業討論約八小時。為配合臨床實習之學習效果，特設計相關之實習作業計有七類：讀書報告、期刊閱讀、團體治療、活動分析、個案研究報告、治療器材或輔具介紹、家庭訪視報告，各有專人負責指導，相信更能豐富學生所學。
課程目標:
實習結束後，學生應具備以下能力：
1. 依理論正確評估個案的功能
2. 設立適當的治療目標
3. 正確設定治療計劃
4. 適當的執行治療
5. 提供適當的出院計畫及準備
6. 具備適當的專業溝通能力與倫理
課程要求: 詳細參考大四臨床實習學生手冊。

課程概述:
本課程目的在於透過聆聽研究者分享的研究歷程，學習研究過程思辨與成果發表之能力。學生透過口頭報告的準備、分享、討論與回饋過程，形成自己研究的計畫、改善研究設計或修正精進研究成果，以提升研究能力、教學能力、專業能力與表達能力。口頭報告以英文分享為主。

授課方式包含：專家演講、學生報告與討論、教師講評。
本課程每學年第二學期開授，所有碩博班教師皆參與。博士班學生於就學期間，需修習2次（4學分）。碩士班學生於就學期間，需修習1次（2學分）。
課程目標:
一、碩班：透過口頭與書面報告及討論，培養學生學術發表與交流討論之能力，包括：
   1.「研究問題的形成」，藉由文獻回顧探討相關此研究問題的重要性。
   2.「針對研究問題提出研究方法」，藉著課堂上的討論，讓參與學生及教師給予意見，修正及補強，參與學生學習如何分析及解決問題。


二、博班：透過口頭報告及討論，培養學生學術口頭發表與交流討論之能力，以及針對自己的博士班研究內容，提出具體之思辨以及論證。可選擇之形式如下：
  1.  分享初步研究構想：研究問題的形成及此研究問題的重要性，並提出初步之研究計畫（tentative proposal）。
  2.  分享博士班研究計畫：可試著提出博士論文計畫書，預演博士論文計畫書審查，參與學生及教師可給予意見讓報告學生學習如何defense及知道自己如何修正及補強自己的計畫書，參與學生也可學習計畫書撰寫及不同思維之問題解決方式。
  3.  「pilot study」研究成果的呈現：學生試著將初步的研究成果呈現，試著討論結果，讓參與學生及教師給予意見，修正及補強研究方法、統計、結果呈現及討論，參與學生學習如何分析及解決問題。
  4.  「研究成果之發表」：學生試著將完整的研究結果呈現，投稿前的試金石，讓參與學生及教師給予意見，修正及補強文章內容，參與學生學習如何撰寫正式的研究文章。

1.基本技術：握拍、執球、熟悉球感、簡易步法、發球、正手高遠長球、平球、切球、網前小
球、挑球、撲球。
2.綜合技術：分組個人排名賽，雙打友誼賽，比賽可以增進基本技術的應用性，增加樂趣與
挑戰性。

歡迎對羽球運動有興趣者及初階學習者參加課程 ( 非初學者需多協助初學者 )。
課程目標:
1.認識初階羽球運動。
2.學習羽球初階基本技巧。
3.學習羽球初階基本技戰術應用單、雙打比賽練習。
4.享受打羽球運動、練習比賽、擔任裁判、啦啦隊...等樂趣與分責技巧練習。
5.交朋友。
課程要求:
本課程本學期將無進行公開抽籤加簽，不提供換班。視當天學生人數及場地情況自行彈加幾位，課中協商 (*114-2學期將不再公開抽學生證加簽(欲加簽同學請勿浪費時間)，保留加簽人數太多時，教師得以當天視情況決定)，選上課程者須身著運動服、室內球鞋(羽球鞋為最佳)、需自備球拍與自備1筒羽球上課必用)。教師同意加簽者當天給加簽授權碼，並請盡快於當天課程中完成登錄 (加選時請留下基本資料及確定有索取授權碼，並登記無誤)。加簽條件需有相當羽球經驗並有意願協助班級課務及餵球給初學者，亦需自備球拍與羽球，條件與前述同。已選上課程者第1次上課無故未出席(含遲到10分鐘以上)未告知緣由者視為退選(上課10分鐘後點名，無故未出席者視為退選名額，提供為當天候補名。因故無法參與第1堂課者，需事先請假，否則，視為退選。課程參與從第一周開始。敬請配合! !


請上課同學穿著運動服裝、室內球鞋(羽球鞋為最佳)、備好羽球球拍、羽球1筒(12顆)、水、毛巾...等，當天加簽的同學亦同。

1. 需填寫成績表（需照片乙張(可看出個人影像之生活照即可)，請於第一次、第二次上課帶來）。
2. 室內課程需著室內羽球鞋（或僅在室內穿著之室內運動鞋），禁止穿著高跟鞋、皮鞋或室外球鞋(請妥善處理)(綜合體育館規定)。

5. 請自行攜帶個人毛巾、水、保暖外套及換洗衣物。
